text:
navin: Heads-up — we're running bring-up for Novelis-8B-compact on dedicated (first pass of quantization). Quick legal check: can we ship 4-bit quantized weights to customers, and are there any attribution/labeling requirements if we host a quantized variant?

lee: short engineering summary — FP32 -> 4-bit (awq) reduced median p95 latency 2.6x and cost/unit ~2.8x improvement. Eval suite (w/ curated prompts) shows a BLEU-like drop for a few instruction categories: avg quality delta = -3.8% (not catastrophic, but visible on long-form summarization).

navin: thanks. main question is redistribution + UI attribution. Some of the source repo has a license that mentions "no binary redistribution without attribution" — not sure how that maps to shipping quantized weights.

sarah (legal): can you paste the exact license excerpt? high-level: we need to know whether the model license treats quantized weights as a derivative or a transformation. if derivative, there may be attribution and redistribution constraints. if transformation, maybe allowed.

navin: pasted below (from upstream LICENSE.txt):

ci-bot: ```
Copyright 2025 Novelis Research
Licensed under the Novelis Noncommercial and Attribution License v1.0
You may use and modify the base weights for noncommercial research only.
Redistribution (including modified or quantized binaries) requires explicit attribution and a redistribution notice.
Commercial deployment or hosting requires express permission.
```

tara: oh — that last line looks like a commercial restriction. we need clarification: is hosting an API considered "commercial deployment"? our customers on hosted product pay for usage, so likely yes.

lee: from an engineering POV we can keep the quantized variant internal on dedicated/private only, but customers would request dedicated hosting. If the license bars hosting for commercial use, we might need a permission or choose another model.

navin: Also question about attribution text: if redistribution is allowed with attribution, does the UI/referral need to show the upstream model name/version? e.g., "powered by Novelis-8B-compact (quantized) — attribution: Novelis Research" somewhere in TOS or app footer?

sarah (legal): attribution is often satisfied by a visible credit and a redistribution notice in docs and the endpoint terms. For embedding in the UI, we can add a brief credit in the model metadata panel and include the full notice in our legal page. But the bigger blocker is the commercial deployment sentence. We need to escalate: ask upstream for a commercial license or a special hosting carve-out.

lee: operational question — if we ask for permission, how long are we willing to hold this from customers? We have internal quant experiments and a canary for latency-sensitive routes. Could we keep a research-only flagged build for internal evals and restrict any external access until license is cleared?

navin: yes, plan = research-only internal cluster + no customer-facing endpoints until legal ok. Meanwhile run evals across our SOTA prompt set, and document regressions.

tara: can someone draft a short outreach email to Novelis Research asking for permission to host a quantized variant for commercial customers, proposing: (1) attribution in UI, (2) backlink to license text, (3) limited logging retention, (4) revenue share / fee if required. I'll help with wording.

navin: I'll assemble perf/quality numbers + sample prompts + PR to legal.

lee: quick technical note for the outreach — include that our quantization is deterministic AWQ 4-bit per-channel, we keep a compatibility layer that can reconstruct a float-like output and we won't publish the quantized binary externally unless permitted. Mention canary rollback and fallback to FP32 upstream if regressions spike.

ci-bot: reminder — internal policy: tag model on onboarding sheet with "legal: pending" and lock the "publish" checkbox until cleared.

sarah (legal): action items from legal: 1) navin — upload the full upstream LICENSE file and hash; 2) tara + sarah — draft the outreach; 3) lee — document exact quant pipeline and a statement we won't redistribute binaries without permission; 4) product — prepare fallback plan for customers. We'll triage with engineering next Tue.

navin: done, uploaded license + eval artifacts to /onboard/novelis-8b-compact/ (internal link). pinging @tara when draft ready. :thumbsup:

lee: rough eval numbers attached in thread: 4-bit AWQ: quality -3.8% (long-form), -1.1% (QA), latency p95 2.6x better. ML note: degradation concentrated on repeated-constraint generation. working on prompt-conditioning mitigation.

tara: ok filing an outbound template. If Novelis declines commercial hosting, fallback plan: recommend customers run Novelis themselves via BYO model on Private offering or use a differently-licensed open model.

navin: thanks team. will wait for legal draft then open outreach. keeping thread open for any other red flags. :wave:
